notes.decision: Restored tentatively as 'the Four Fathers' since ⲛⲓⲱⲧ 'fathers' is the most common -ⲱⲧ ending word and Manichaean cosmology has the Five Fathers structure (with sub-grouping of four possible). However, the body of the chapter does not directly enumerate four fathers; it discusses correspondences of body/Greatness/cosmos/soul. The number 'four' in the title may govern a structure not yet articulated in the preserved portion. Confidence low.

The relative ⲉⲧⲉⲣⲉ governs the feminine †ⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁⲟ̄ 'the Greatness.' Construction completes on line 14 with ⲧⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲛⲧ̄ ⲙⲙⲁⲥ 'we liken her' — i.e., 'this in which we liken the entire Greatness.' The dagger † here is the editor's mark for the ϯ ligature (ϯ-ⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁⲟ̄ — though ⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁⲟ̄ is feminine and would not normally take ϯ; possibly ⲡ-).

Translated 'this place of emptiness which is outside.' ⲙⲁⲛⲭⲁⲓⲉ = ⲙⲁ-ⲛ-ϫⲁⲉⲓⲉ 'place of desert/wilderness/emptiness' — the cosmos understood as the desolate outer region beyond the Father's hidden kingdom. NOT to be read as ⲙⲁⲛⲓⲭⲁⲓⲟⲥ 'Manichaean,' which is grammatically and theologically impossible here.

Translated 'they are alike, alike to the two eyes of the body.' The form ⲟⲓⲣⲁⲩ ⲟⲓⲣⲟ is opaque; tentatively analyzed as a comparative-copular doublet (3pl + 3sg) expressing equivalence between the two ships of light and the two eyes of the body. Possible alternatives: 'their counterpart, his counterpart [is] the two eyes' (cf. ⲟⲉⲣⲏⲟ 'counterpart' in glossary), or a verb of resemblance. Confidence low; flagged for parallel attestations.

Translated 'the parts of the flesh.' The doubled † (ϯ ligature) likely renders ⲧϯⲉ 'portion/half' (in glossary) doubled or ⲧ-ϯⲡⲉ 'the kinds/tastes,' yielding 'the portions/parts/senses of the flesh' as agents that destroy the soul. The semantic field is the bodily faculties/parts that war against the soul — Manichaean anthropological commonplace. Specific reading uncertain.

Untranslated as the start; this is the continuation of a word from the previous page (no lacuna marker on this page). The visible '...ⲱⲛ ⲛ̄ⲃⲣ̄ⲡⲉ' may be the end of a compound such as ⲡⲣⲙⲛⲃⲣ̄ⲡⲉ 'the New Man' (in glossary) or ⲡⲧⲁⲓⲱⲛ ⲛ̄ⲃⲣ̄ⲡⲉ 'the New Aeon' (in glossary). The closing line 4 'before God and the apostles' suggests the ending of a doxological/ethical conclusion to the previous kephalaion.

Translated 'the teaching of the body' preserving the mandatory rendering of ⲥⲃⲱ as 'teaching.' The construction here is unusual — perhaps designating an inner instructional principle within the body (as the soul or Mind of Light's instruction concealed within), parallel to the Father hidden within his kingship. This functions as the analogical middle term in a three-tier correspondence: body-members ↔ teaching-of-body ↔ Father-in-kingdom.
